children.translated_text:
The <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtras</s> (Aphorisms on the Ornaments of Poetry),
composed by the eminent scholar <s>Śrī Vāmana</s>,
together with his own commentary (<s>svavṛtti</s>).
The first topic (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>), called '<s>Śārīra</s>' (The Body [of Poetry]).
Chapter One.
Having bowed to the supreme light, by <s>Vāmana</s>, dear to poets,
a commentary (<s>vṛtti</s>) on those <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtras</s> is composed.
Poetry (<s>kāvya</s>) is to be valued for its ornamentation (<s>alaṅkāra</s>). (1.1.1)
Beauty (<s>saundarya</s>) is ornamentation. (1.1.2)
That [beauty arises] through the avoidance of faults (<s>doṣas</s>) and the adoption of qualities (<s>guṇas</s>) and ornaments (<s>alaṅkāras</s>). (1.1.3)
Those [avoidance and adoption] are learned from treatises (<s>śāstra</s>). (1.1.4)
Poetry serves both visible and invisible purposes, because it is the cause of pleasure and fame. (1.1.5)
Chapter Two.
Poets are of two kinds: the fastidious (<s>arocakin</s>) and those who consume along with the grass (<s>satṛṇābhyavahārin</s>). (1.2.1)
The former are [true] disciples, because of their discernment. (1.2.2)
Not the latter, because of the opposite [quality]. (1.2.3)
A treatise is not purposeful with regard to things devoid of [poetic] substance. (1.2.4)
Nor is the clearing-nut (<s>kataka</s>) for purifying mud. (1.2.5)
<s>Rīti</s> (style) is the soul of poetry. (1.2.6)
<s>Rīti</s> is a distinctive arrangement of words. (1.2.7)
The distinction is constituted by <s>guṇas</s> (qualities). (1.2.8)

children.text: sā tridhā --- vaidarbhī gauḍīyā pāñcālī ceti // VKal_1,2.9 //
children.translated_text: It [<s>rīti</s>] is threefold — <s>Vaidarbhī</s>, <s>Gauḍīyā</s>, and <s>Pāñcālī</s>. (1.2.9)
They are named after <s>Vidarbha</s> and the other [regions], because they are observed [there]. (1.2.10)
The <s>Vaidarbhī</s> possesses all the <s>guṇas</s> together. (1.2.11)
The <s>Gauḍīyā</s> possesses <s>ojas</s> (vigor) and <s>kānti</s> (luster). (1.2.12)
The <s>Pāñcālī</s> is endowed with <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) and <s>saukumārya</s> (delicacy). (1.2.13)
Among them, the first [<s>Vaidarbhī</s>] is to be preferred, because of its completeness of <s>guṇas</s>. (1.2.14)
Not the others, however, because of their paucity of <s>guṇas</s>. (1.2.15)
Some say that practice of the others is for the purpose of ascending to that [<s>Vaidarbhī</s>]. (1.2.16)
But that is not so; for one habituated to non-truth does not arrive at truth. (1.2.17)
By practicing with hemp-thread on a loom, one does not gain the diversity of silk-thread. (1.2.18)
That [<s>Vaidarbhī</s>], in the absence of compounds, is the pure <s>Vaidarbhī</s>. (1.2.19)
In it, the excellence of meaning-qualities is to be relished. (1.2.20)
By building upon that, even a trace of meaning-quality [suffices]. (1.2.21)
That too is [called] <s>Vaidarbhī</s>, by virtue of being dependent on it. (1.2.22)
Chapter Three.

children.text: loko vidyā prakīrṇa ca kāvyāṅgāni // VKal_1,3.1 //
children.translated_text: The constituents of poetry are worldly experience (<s>loka</s>), learned disciplines (<s>vidyā</s>), and miscellaneous [factors] (<s>prakīrṇa</s>). (1.3.1)
Worldly conduct is '<s>loka</s>' (worldly experience). (1.3.2)

The learned disciplines begin with grammar (<s>śabdasmṛti</s>), lexicon (<s>abhidhānakośa</s>), prosody (<s>chandoviciti</s>), arts (<s>kalā</s>), the science of love (<s>kāmaśāstra</s>), and statecraft (<s>daṇḍanīti</s>). (1.3.3)
From grammar comes purity of language. (1.3.4)
From the lexicon comes certainty of word-meanings. (1.3.5)
From prosody comes the resolution of doubts regarding meters. (1.3.6)
From the treatises on arts comes knowledge of the true nature of the arts. (1.3.7)
From the science of love, [knowledge of] the conduct of love. (1.3.8)
From statecraft, [knowledge of] policy and the absence of policy. (1.3.9)
And from it [also comes knowledge of] the intricacies of narrative. (1.3.10)

children.text: lakṣyajñatvamabhiyogo vṛddhasevāvekṣaṇaṃ pratibhānamavadhānaṃ ca prakīrṇam // VKal_1,3.11 //
children.translated_text: The miscellaneous [factors] are: acquaintance with models (<s>lakṣyajñatva</s>), endeavor (<s>abhiyoga</s>), attendance upon elders (<s>vṛddhasevā</s>), reflection (<s>avekṣaṇa</s>), creative inspiration (<s>pratibhāna</s>), and concentration (<s>avadhāna</s>). (1.3.11)
Therein, acquaintance with models is familiarity with poetry. (1.3.12)
Endeavor is the exertion of composing poetry. (1.3.13)
Attendance upon elders is service to a teacher of poetic instruction. (1.3.14)
Reflection is the placing and removing of words. (1.3.15)
Creative inspiration (<s>pratibhāna</s>) is the seed of poetic genius. (1.3.16)
Concentration (<s>avadhāna</s>) is single-pointedness of mind. (1.3.17)
That [concentration depends] on place and time. (1.3.18)
A secluded place is [appropriate]. (1.3.19)
The fourth watch of the night is the [appropriate] time. (1.3.20)
Poetry is of two kinds: prose (<s>gadya</s>) and verse (<s>padya</s>). (1.3.21)
Prose is of three kinds: that which has the flavor of verse (<s>vṛttagandhi</s>), flowing prose (<s>cūrṇa</s>), and that which mainly consists of elaborate periods (<s>utkalikāprāya</s>). (1.3.22)
That which contains portions of verse is <s>vṛttagandhi</s>. (1.3.23)
Flowing prose (<s>cūrṇa</s>) has uncompounded, graceful words. (1.3.24)
The opposite is <s>utkalikāprāya</s>. (1.3.25)
Verse (<s>padya</s>) has many varieties. (1.3.26)
It is either unconnected (<s>anibaddha</s>) or connected (<s>nibaddha</s>). (1.3.27)
The progressive perfection of these two is like a garland and a crest-jewel. (1.3.28)
An unconnected [verse] does not shine [by itself], like an atom of a single radiance. (1.3.29)
Among connected compositions, the tenfold dramatic form (<s>daśarūpaka</s>) is best. (1.3.30)
For it is variegated, like a painted canvas, because of the completeness of its distinctive [elements]. (1.3.31)
From that, the classification of other varieties [is derived]. (1.3.32)
Thus concludes the first topic, called '<s>Śārīra</s>' (The Body).
The second topic, called '<s>Doṣadarśana</s>' (The Examination of Faults).
Chapter One.
Faults (<s>doṣas</s>) are the opposite in nature of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities). (2.1.1)
Their comprehension is through meaning. (2.1.2)
Elaboration [is given] for ease [of understanding]. (2.1.3)

children.text: duṣṭaṃ padamasādhu kaṣṭaṃ grāmyamapratītamanarthakaṃ ca // VKal_2,1.4 //
children.translated_text: A faulty word is one that is improper (<s>asādhu</s>), harsh (<s>kaṣṭa</s>), vulgar (<s>grāmya</s>), unfamiliar (<s>apratīta</s>), or meaningless (<s>anarthaka</s>). (2.1.4)
'Improper' (<s>asādhu</s>) means contrary to grammar (<s>śabdasmṛti</s>). (2.1.5)
'Harsh' (<s>kaṣṭa</s>) means offensive to the ear. (2.1.6)
'Vulgar' (<s>grāmya</s>) means employed only in common usage. (2.1.7)
'Unfamiliar' (<s>apratīta</s>) means employed only in treatises. (2.1.8)
'Meaningless' (<s>anarthaka</s>) means [used merely] for the purpose of padding. (2.1.9)
Not [meaningless] if for the purpose of a figure of speech (<s>vākyālaṅkāra</s>). (2.1.10)
[Further word-faults:] requiring another meaning (<s>anyārthaneyam</s>), having obscure meaning (<s>gūḍhārtha</s>), indecent (<s>aślīla</s>), and forced (<s>kliṣṭa</s>). (2.1.11)
'Requiring another meaning' means deviating from conventional usage (<s>rūḍhi</s>). (2.1.12)
'Having a contrived meaning' is 'requiring interpretation' (<s>neyārtha</s>). (2.1.13)
'Having obscure meaning' means employing a sense that is not well known. (2.1.14)
'Indecent' (<s>aślīla</s>) is that which suggests an improper secondary meaning or an improper reminiscence. (2.1.15)
Not [indecent are] the concealed (<s>gupta</s>), the marked (<s>lakṣita</s>), and the veiled (<s>saṃvṛta</s>). (2.1.16)
'Concealed' (<s>gupta</s>) means indecent through an unfamiliar [expression]. (2.1.17)
'Marked' (<s>lakṣita</s>) means having a figuratively indecent accompaniment. (2.1.18)
'Veiled' (<s>saṃvṛta</s>) means covered by common usage. (2.1.19)
That [indecency] is threefold, due to the distinction of [expressions] causing shame, disgust, or inauspiciousness. (2.1.20)
'Forced' (<s>kliṣṭa</s>) means requiring a detached cognition to grasp its meaning. (2.1.21)
By the last two [indecent and forced], the sentence is also characterized [as faulty]. (2.1.22)
Chapter Two.
Sentences [are faulty when they are] broken in meter (<s>bhinnavṛtta</s>), deviating in caesura (<s>yatibhraṣṭa</s>), or having faulty juncture (<s>visaṃdhi</s>). (2.2.1)
'Broken in meter' means a meter that has departed from its defining characteristics. (2.2.2)
'Deviating in caesura' means having an unpleasant pause. (2.2.3)
That [faulty caesura occurs] generally through an unsanctioned junction of a verbal root, a noun, or a word-segment with a vowel-sandhi. (2.2.4)
A caesura-fault is not a fault separate from meter-fault, since meter is constituted by caesura. (2.2.5)
[Objection:] No, because their definitions are distinct. (2.2.6)
Faulty juncture (<s>visaṃdhi</s>) is an ugly joining of words. (2.2.7)
The ugliness of word-juncture consists of disjunction, indecency, and harshness. (2.2.8)

[Sentence-faults further include:] redundancy (<s>vyartha</s>), tautology (<s>ekārtha</s>), ambiguity (<s>saṃdigdha</s>), inconsistency (<s>ayukta</s>), inversion (<s>apakrama</s>), and contradiction with worldly experience or learned disciplines. (2.2.9)
'Redundancy' means having a contradictory preceding and succeeding meaning. (2.2.10)
'Tautology' means having words that express an already-stated meaning. (2.2.11)
[Objection:] No, if there is a [meaningful] distinction, [what appears as] tautology is not faulty. (2.2.12)
In the sounds of 'bowstring' and 'bow,' the word 'bow' [separately] is for the sake of the well-established understanding. (2.2.13)
In 'ear-ornament,' 'ear-ring,' 'ear-pendant,' and 'head-crest,' the mention of 'ear' and the like is because of proximity. (2.2.14)
In the word '<s>muktāhāra</s>' (pearl necklace), the word '<s>muktā</s>' (pearl) is for purity. (2.2.15)
In the word '<s>puṣpamālā</s>' (flower garland), the word '<s>puṣpa</s>' (flower) is for excellence. (2.2.16)
In the word '<s>karikalabha</s>' (elephant calf), the word '<s>kari</s>' (elephant) is for specification. (2.2.17)
And [also] as a qualifier. (2.2.18)
This [exception applies] in established usage. (2.2.19)
'Ambiguous' means producing doubt. (2.2.20)
An expression with a contrived meaning, as in 'māyā' (illusion) and the like, is 'inconsistent.' (2.2.21)
'Inversion' (<s>apakrama</s>) means having its meaning out of sequence. (2.2.22)
Statements with meanings contradicting place, time, and nature are contrary to worldly experience. (2.2.23)
Statements with meanings contradicting the arts, the four aims of life, and the [other] treatises are contrary to learned disciplines. (2.2.24)
Thus concludes the second topic, called '<s>Doṣadarśana</s>' (The Examination of Faults).
The third topic, called '<s>Guṇavivecana</s>' (The Discrimination of Qualities).
Chapter One.
<s>Guṇas</s> (qualities) are the properties that produce the beauty of poetry. (3.1.1)
The causes of their enhancement, however, are the <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments). (3.1.2)
The former [<s>guṇas</s>] are permanent. (3.1.3)

The qualities of composition (<s>bandhaguṇas</s>) are: <s>ojas</s> (vigor), <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity), <s>śleṣa</s> (cohesion), <s>samatā</s> (evenness), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration/propriety), <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), <s>saukumārya</s> (delicacy), <s>udāratā</s> (nobility), <s>arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning), and <s>kānti</s> (luster). (3.1.4)
<s>Ojas</s> (vigor) is tightness of composition. (3.1.5)
<s>Prasāda</s> (lucidity) is looseness [of composition]. (3.1.6)
[It is a] <s>guṇa</s> because of [the resulting overall] blending. (3.1.7)
It, however, is established through experience. (3.1.8)
And [through] equality and superiority. (3.1.9)
<s>Śleṣa</s> (cohesion) is smoothness. (3.1.10)
Non-divergence from the style (<s>mārga</s>) is <s>samatā</s> (evenness). // VKal 3.1.11 //
The order of ascent and descent is <s>samādhi</s> (arrangement). // VKal 3.1.12 //
[<s>Samādhi</s> is] not separate [from <s>ojas</s> and <s>prasāda</s>], since ascent and descent have the nature of <s>ojas</s> and <s>prasāda</s>. // VKal 3.1.13* //
No, because they are not intermixed. // VKal 3.1.14* //
And because there is no invariable concomitance. // VKal 3.1.15 //
If one grants that [<s>samādhi</s> is] the intense state of <s>ojas</s> and <s>prasāda</s>, then those [would suffice]. // VKal 3.1.16* //
Because those two depend on a [further] distinction. // VKal 3.1.17 //
<s>Samādhi</s> is so called because it denotes the cause of ascent and descent. // VKal 3.1.18 //
Or, for the purpose of prescribing order. // VKal 3.1.19 //
Separateness of words is <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness). // VKal 3.1.20 //
Absence of harshness is <s>saukumārya</s> (delicacy). // VKal 3.1.21 //
Grandeur is <s>udāratā</s> (sublimity). // VKal 3.1.22 //
Being the cause of clarity of meaning is <s>arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning). // VKal 3.1.23 //
Brilliance is <s>kānti</s> (lustre). // VKal 3.1.24 //
[These qualities] are not nonexistent, because they are cognizable by the discerning. // VKal 3.1.25* //
[They are] not illusory, because they are unshakable. // VKal 3.1.26* //
[They are] not [mere] features of recitation, because [they are] not observed everywhere. // VKal 3.1.27* //
Second Chapter.
Those very ones are the qualities of meaning (<s>arthaguṇas</s>). // VKal 3.2.1 //
Robustness of meaning is <s>ojas</s> (vigor). // VKal 3.2.2 //
Purity of meaning is <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity). // VKal 3.2.3 //
Coherence is <s>śleṣa</s> (compactness). // VKal 3.2.4 //
Absence of disparity is <s>samatā</s> (evenness). // VKal 3.2.5 //
Insight into meaning is <s>samādhi</s> (arrangement). // VKal 3.2.6 //
Meaning is twofold: that which is not a source, or that which is the source of another shade [of meaning]. // VKal 3.2.7* //
Meaning is [either] manifest or subtle. // VKal 3.2.8 //
The subtle [meaning] is to be contemplated and to be suggested. // VKal 3.2.9 //
Variety of expression is <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness). // VKal 3.2.10 //
Absence of harshness is <s>saukumārya</s> (delicacy). // VKal 3.2.11 //
Freedom from vulgarity is <s>udāratā</s> (sublimity). // VKal 3.2.12 //
Distinctness of the intrinsic nature of the subject is <s>arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning). // VKal 3.2.13 //
Radiant aesthetic sentiment (<s>rasa</s>) is <s>kānti</s> (lustre). // VKal 3.2.14 //
Thus concludes the discussion of qualities (<s>guṇavivecana</s>), the third section (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>).
The fourth section, named '<s>Ālaṅkārika</s>' (On Ornaments).
First Chapter.
A word that is not of a single meaning, or an unrepeated syllable, restricted to a [particular] position, is <s>yamaka</s> (rhyming). // VKal 4.1.1 //
The positions are: the beginning, middle, and end portions of one foot (<s>pāda</s>) or of several feet. // VKal 4.1.2 //
From [syllabic] splitting (<s>bhaṅga</s>) arises excellence. // VKal 4.1.3 //
<s>Śṛṅkhalā</s> (chain), <s>parivartaka</s> (reversal), and <s>cūrṇa</s> (powder) — these are the modes of splitting. // VKal 4.1.4 //
The movement by separation of syllables (<s>varṇaviccheda</s>) is <s>śṛṅkhalā</s> (chain). // VKal 4.1.5 //
When the combination is dissolved, the appearance of the original form is <s>parivartaka</s> (reversal). // VKal 4.1.6 //
When a cluster of syllables is broken and the original form is lost, it is <s>cūrṇa</s> (powder). // VKal 4.1.7 //
The remainder, having similar form, is <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration). // VKal 4.1.8 //
A <s>varṇānuprāsa</s> (syllabic alliteration) that is not excessive is preferable. // VKal 4.1.9 //
<s>Pādānuprāsa</s> (foot-alliteration) is like foot-<s>yamaka</s>. // VKal 4.1.10 //
Second Chapter.
The partial similarity of the object of comparison (<s>upameya</s>) with the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) in respect of a quality is <s>upamā</s> (simile). // VKal 4.2.1 //
And from an abundance of qualities, an imagined [simile] (<s>kalpitā</s>). // VKal 4.2.2 //
Its twofold [nature arises] from the distinction of word-sense, sentence-sense, and figurative usage. // VKal 4.2.3* //
It is [either] complete (<s>pūrṇā</s>) or elliptical (<s>luptā</s>). // VKal 4.2.4 //
When there is a complete set of the quality-indicating word, the standard of comparison, and the object of comparison, it is complete (<s>pūrṇā</s>). // VKal 4.2.5 //
When [any of these is] omitted, it is elliptical (<s>luptā</s>). // VKal 4.2.6 //
[Simile occurs] in praise, censure, and statement of fact. // VKal 4.2.7 //
Inferiority, superiority, discrepancy in gender, discrepancy in number, dissimilarity, and impossibility — these are its faults. // VKal 4.2.8 //
Inferiority of the standard of comparison arises from deficiency in species, magnitude, or attribute. // VKal 4.2.9 //
When one of two attributes is specified, the other is understood from their regular association. // VKal 4.2.10* //
By that, superiority [as a fault] has been explained. // VKal 4.2.11 //
Discrepancy in grammatical gender between the standard and the object of comparison is <s>liṅgabheda</s> (gender-fault). // VKal 4.2.12 //
It is generally acceptable between masculine and neuter. // VKal 4.2.13 //
[It is acceptable] in conventional [usage], in compounds, and in elaborated similes. // VKal 4.2.14 //
By that, discrepancy in number (<s>vacanabheda</s>) has been explained. // VKal 4.2.15 //
Similarity in a quality that is not well-known is dissimilarity (<s>asādṛśya</s>). // VKal 4.2.16 //
A simile is indeed ruined by dissimilarity, and poets rest upon that [principle]. // VKal 4.2.17* //
From the superiority of the standard of comparison, some say it is a removal of that [fault]. // VKal 4.2.18 //
No, because it would have an unsupported meaning. // VKal 4.2.19* //
Logical impossibility is <s>asaṃbhava</s> (non-occurrence). // VKal 4.2.20 //
Hyperbole (<s>atiśaya</s>) is not contradictory [to simile]. // VKal 4.2.21 //
Third Chapter.
<s>Prativastu</s> (counter-subject) and so forth constitute the elaboration of simile (<s>upamāprapañca</s>). // VKal 4.3.1 //
When the object of comparison is stated, the juxtaposition of a similar subject is <s>prativastu</s> (counter-subject). // VKal 4.3.2 //
When [the object of comparison] is not stated, it is <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression). // VKal 4.3.3 //
When something is partially stated, it is <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant). // VKal 4.3.4 //
The denial of [identity] by substituting a similar object is <s>apahṇuti</s> (concealment). // VKal 4.3.5 //
The superimposition of identity upon the object of comparison due to complete similarity in qualities with the standard is <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor). // VKal 4.3.6 //
That [superimposition], when applied to attributes in a composite way, is <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia). // VKal 4.3.7 //
A figurative expression (<s>vakrokti</s>) based on resemblance is <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication). // VKal 4.3.8 //
The imagining of something as other than its true nature, for the purpose of exaggeration, is <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy). // VKal 4.3.9 //
The imagining of excellence of a possible attribute is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole). // VKal 4.3.10 //
Doubt between the standard and the object of comparison is <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt). // VKal 4.3.11 //
The appearance of contradiction is <s>virodha</s> (contradiction). // VKal 4.3.12 //
When an action is negated yet its well-known result is manifest, it is <s>vibhāvanā</s> (causeless production). // VKal 4.3.13 //
When a single thing serves as both the object and the standard of comparison, it is <s>ananvaya</s> (self-comparison). // VKal 4.3.14 //
In succession, [there is] <s>upameyopamā</s> (reciprocal simile). // VKal 4.3.15 //
The exchange [of roles] between similar and dissimilar [things] is <s>parivṛtti</s> (interchange). // VKal 4.3.16 //
The sequential connection of objects of comparison and standards of comparison is <s>krama</s> (succession). // VKal 4.3.17 //
A single action common to sentences containing both the standard and the object of comparison is <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination). // VKal 4.3.18 //
The indication, through an action alone, of its connection with one's own and another's purpose is <s>nidarśana</s> (illustration). // VKal 4.3.20 //
That is threefold, from the distinction of occurrence at the beginning, middle, or end of the sentence. // VKal 4.3.19* //
The introduction of another matter altogether for the purpose of establishing the [original] statement is <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration). // VKal 4.3.21 //
The superiority of the object of comparison in quality is <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast). // VKal 4.3.22 //
When the loss of one quality is imagined, the strengthening of equality [in another] is <s>viśeṣokti</s> (distinction). // VKal 4.3.23 //
Praise or censure expressed through the non-performance of a possible distinguished action is <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise). // VKal 4.3.24 //
When the pretense resembles truth, it is <s>vyājokti</s> (feigned expression). // VKal 4.3.25 //
The simultaneous occurrence of actions for the purpose of showing equality with something distinguished is <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal association). // VKal 4.3.26 //
The rejection of the standard of comparison is <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection). // VKal 4.3.27 //
The expression of two simultaneous subjects and actions in a single word is <s>sahokti</s> (co-expression). // VKal 4.3.28 //
Whatever resemblance attains identity, that, being realized, is <s>saṃpatti</s> (consummation). // VKal 4.3.29 //
When one ornament becomes the source of another ornament, it is <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination). // VKal 4.3.30 //
Its two varieties are: the component-of-simile-and-metaphor (<s>upamārūpaka</s>) and the component-of-poetic-fancy (<s>utprekṣāvayava</s>). // VKal 4.3.31 //
A metaphor generated from simile is <s>upamārūpaka</s>. // VKal 4.3.32 //
The cause of poetic fancy is <s>utprekṣāvayava</s> (component of poetic fancy). // VKal 4.3.33 //
Thus concludes '<s>Ālaṅkārika</s>' (On Ornaments), the fourth section.
The fifth section, named '<s>Prāyogika</s>' (On Practice).
First Chapter.

children.text: naikaṃ padaṃ dviḥ prayojyaṃ prāyeṇa // VKal_5,1.1 //
children.translated_text: Generally, a single word should not be used twice. // VKal 5.1.1 //
<s>Sandhi</s> (euphonic combination) is always [to be applied], as with a single word in verses, except at the mid-point of [a verse]. // VKal 5.1.2 //
A light syllable at the end of a foot should not [be treated as] heavy anywhere. // VKal 5.1.3 //

children.text: na gādye samāptaprāyaṃ vṛttam, anyatrodgatādibhyaḥ saṃvādāt // VKal_5,1.4* //
children.translated_text: In verse composition (<s>gādya</s>), a meter that is nearly complete should not [be used], except when it agrees with <s>Udgatā</s> and the like. // VKal 5.1.4* //
<s>Khalu</s> and similar [particles] should not [appear] at the beginning of a foot. // VKal 5.1.5 //
A complete sentence should not [end] at the half-[verse]. // VKal 5.1.6 //
A <s>karmadhāraya</s> (descriptive compound) should not produce [an erroneous] <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (possessive compound) interpretation. // VKal 5.1.7 //
By that, the converse has also been explained. // VKal 5.1.8 //
When the negation of a possible [thing] is to be reversed, two negations [are used]. // VKal 5.1.9 //
The use of a qualifier alone [is sufficient] for the understanding of the qualified. // VKal 5.1.10 //
A pronoun serves to connect [with] what is concealed by the [compound] formation. // VKal 5.1.11 //
The genitive case is sometimes used even for a secondary relation. // VKal 5.1.12 //
A word from a regional dialect that is overused [should be avoided]. // VKal 5.1.13 //
[Faults include:] grammatical gender [errors] and ellipsis [of words]. // VKal 5.1.14 //
And [the same for] figurative expressions and [unusual] words. // VKal 5.1.15 //
There should not be an excess of those in a single [passage]. // VKal 5.1.16 //
The class [designation] of <s>stana</s> (breast) and similar [words expressed in] dual is generally [to be treated as] the species. // VKal 5.1.17 //
Second Chapter.
The <s>ekaśeṣa</s> (retention of one) [form] in <s>Rudrāv</s> [dual of <s>Rudra</s>] should be investigated. // VKal 5.2.1 //
The verbal root status of <s>milī</s>, <s>klabī</s>, <s>kṣipā</s> and similar [forms] is [to be accepted], since [their] root-quality is not fully established. // VKal 5.2.2* //
The <s>Ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) of [the root] <s>val</s> is not invariable, as indicated by [grammatical] evidence (<s>jñāpaka</s>). // VKal 5.2.3* //
'<s>kṣīyate</s>' (is diminished) — [this is used] in the <s>karmakartar</s> (object-as-agent) construction. (VKal 5.2.4)
And likewise '<s>khidyate</s>' (is afflicted). (VKal 5.2.5)
In [the root] <s>mārg</s> (to seek), the <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) is a grammatical blemish (<s>alakṣma</s>). (VKal 5.2.6)
Forms like '<s>lolamāna</s>' (wavering) etc. [are justified] without the [expected] <s>anaś</s> [suffix]. (VKal 5.2.7)

From [the root] <s>labh</s> (to obtain), since it has the meaning of motion (<s>gatyartha</s>), the <s>ṇic</s> and <s>yaṇ</s> [suffixes apply]; the agent [may take] object-hood or non-object-hood. (VKal 5.2.8)
The words '<s>te</s>' and '<s>me</s>' [are listed] among the particles (<s>nipātas</s>). (VKal 5.2.9*)
'<s>Tiraskṛta</s>' (contemned) [is used] in the sense of '<s>paribhūta</s>' (insulted), through figurative extension of [the sense of] concealment (<s>antardhi</s>). (VKal 5.2.10*)
The word '<s>eka</s>' (one) [does not form a compound in this way], because of [the rule] '<s>sup-sup</s>' governing compound formation (<s>samāsa</s>). (VKal 5.2.11*)
The compound of [words like] '<s>madhupipāsu</s>' (desiring honey) etc. [is justified] because of [their] listing among '<s>gami-gāmi</s>' and similar [forms]. (VKal 5.2.12)
The word '<s>trivalī</s>' (three folds) is established [as correct] if [it is treated as] a proper name (<s>saṃjñā</s>). (VKal 5.2.13)
'<s>Bimbādhara</s>' (bimba-fruit-lip) [is formed] through a compound operation (<s>vṛtti</s>) involving elision of the middle word (<s>madhyamapadalopinī</s>). (VKal 5.2.14)
In [forms like] '<s>āmūlalola</s>' (wavering from the root) etc., the compound operation functions like [that of] '<s>vispaṣṭa</s>' and '<s>paṭu</s>.' (VKal 5.2.15)

children.text: na dhānyaṣaṣṭhādiṣu ṣaṣṭhīsamāsapratiṣedhaḥ, pūraṇena taddhitāntatvāt // VKal_5,2.16* //
children.translated_text: The prohibition of the <s>ṣaṣṭhī</s> (genitive) compound does not apply in [forms like] '<s>dhānyaṣaṣṭha</s>' etc., because [the word is] a <s>taddhitānta</s> (secondary derivative) with a <s>pūraṇa</s> (ordinal) [suffix]. (VKal 5.2.16*)
In [forms like] '<s>patrapīti</s>' etc., [the compound is formed] with a <s>guṇavacana</s> (quality-denoting word). (VKal 5.2.17)
A <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (exocentric compound) with a non-coreferential (<s>vyadhikaraṇa</s>) [relationship], having '<s>janma</s>' (birth) etc. as the latter member, is not to be avoided. (VKal 5.2.18)
[Forms like] '<s>hastāgra</s>' (hand-tip), '<s>agrahasta</s>' (front-hand), etc. [arise] because of the [alternation between] identity and non-identity of the quality and the qualified. (VKal 5.2.19)
In the fronting (<s>pūrvanipāta</s>) [of compound members], deviation (<s>apabhraṃśa</s>) should be guarded against. (VKal 5.2.20)

children.text: nipātenāpyabhihite karmaṇi na karmavibhaktiḥ, parigaṇanasya prāyikatvāt // VKal_5,2.21* //
children.translated_text: Even when the object is expressed by a particle (<s>nipāta</s>), the case-ending for the object (<s>karmavibhakti</s>) [need not apply], since the enumeration [of particles] is only approximate (<s>prāyika</s>). (VKal 5.2.21*)

children.text: śakyamiti rūpaṃ karmābhidhāyāṃ liṅgavacanasyāpi sāmānyopakramāt // VKal_5,2.22 //
children.translated_text: The form '<s>śakyam</s>' (it is possible), when denoting the object (<s>karmābhidhāyā</s>), [takes neuter gender] because of the general approach (<s>sāmānyopakrama</s>) regarding gender and number. (VKal 5.2.22)
Like diminution (<s>hāni</s>), excess (<s>ādhikya</s>) of limbs is also a modification (<s>vikāra</s>). (VKal 5.2.23)
Not [so] for [compounds of] '<s>kṛmi</s>' (worm) and '<s>kīṭa</s>' (insect), because of the unwanted consequence of singular treatment (<s>ekavadbhāva</s>). (VKal 5.2.24*)
Not [so for the pair] '<s>khara</s>-<s>uṣṭra</s>' (donkey-camel), because of the listing [in the grammatical text as] '<s>uṣṭra-khara</s>.' (VKal 5.2.25*)
'<s>Āse</s>' [is derived] from [the root] <s>ās</s> (to sit). (VKal 5.2.26)
'<s>Yudhyet</s>' [is formed] from [the root] <s>yudh</s> (to fight) with the <s>kyac</s> [suffix]. (VKal 5.2.27)
In [forms like] '<s>viralāyamāna</s>' (becoming sparse) etc., the <s>kyaṅ</s> [suffix] is to be analyzed. (VKal 5.2.28)

From [the root] <s>han</s> (to strike), the <s>ṇic</s> [causative suffix applies] even without a causal agent (<s>ahetu</s>), because of [its] listing among the <s>curādi</s> (tenth-class) [roots]. (VKal 5.2.29*)
'<s>Anucarī</s>' (female attendant) — from [the root] <s>car</s> (to move), because of [its having] the <s>iṣṭi</s> suffix [i.e., intended meaning]. (VKal 5.2.30)
The word '<s>kesarālam</s>' — [formed with] the <s>aṇi</s> [suffix] from [the root] <s>al</s>. (VKal 5.2.31)
The word '<s>patralam</s>' (leafy) — [formed with] the [suffix] <s>ke</s> from [the root] <s>lā</s>. (VKal 5.2.32)
[Forms like] '<s>mahīdhra</s>' (mountain, lit. earth-bearer) etc. [are justified] by analogy with [the root compounds] <s>mūlavibhuj</s> etc. (VKal 5.2.33)
In [compounds with] '<s>brahma</s>' etc. as the first member, the restrictive rule for [the root] <s>han</s> [does not prevent formation of] '<s>ariha</s>' etc. (VKal 5.2.34)
[Forms like] '<s>brahmavid</s>' (knower of <s>Brahman</s>) etc. [are formed] through the <s>kṛdanta</s> (verbal derivative) compound operation. (VKal 5.2.35)
By those [same principles], [forms like] '<s>mahīdhara</s>' (mountain) etc. are explained. (VKal 5.2.36)
[Forms like] '<s>bhidura</s>' (fragile) etc. [are used both] in the <s>karmakartar</s> (object-as-agent) [sense] and in the agent [sense]. (VKal 5.2.37)
[Forms like] '<s>guṇavistara</s>' (expanse of qualities) etc. are to be considered [carefully]. (VKal 5.2.38)
The interchange of long and short vowels in the words '<s>avatāra</s>' (descent) and '<s>apacāya</s>' (diminution) is [an error] of the ignorant (<s>bāla</s>). (VKal 5.2.39)
'<s>Śobhe</s>' [is justified] by virtue of being an irregular formation (<s>nipātana</s>). (VKal 5.2.40)

children.text: avidhau guroḥ striyāṃ bahulaṃ vivakṣā // VKal_5,2.41 //
children.translated_text: When not [denoting] a prescription (<s>avidhi</s>), for the heavy [syllable root], in the feminine, there is often (<s>bahulam</s>) [application based on] the speaker's intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>). (VKal 5.2.41)
In [forms like] '<s>vyavasita</s>' (resolved) etc., the <s>kta</s> [past participle suffix is used] in the agent [sense], because of the [optional] word '<s>ca</s>.' (VKal 5.2.42*)

'<s>Āha</s>' (he said) — in the past tense, [it is] from [the root] <s>brū</s> (to speak), in the <s>laṭ</s> (present tense) [paradigm], through the error of [confusing it with] another <s>aṇ</s>-ending [root]. (VKal 5.2.43)
From [stems like] '<s>śabala</s>' (variegated) etc., the <s>ṭāp</s> [feminine suffix] does not obtain for the feminine. (VKal 5.2.44)
'<s>Nīlā</s>' (dark blue) when [applied to] a living being (<s>prāṇin</s>) — this is to be considered [carefully]. (VKal 5.2.45)
For [the word] '<s>manuṣyajāti</s>' (human race), [either] expression or non-expression [of gender] [is possible]. (VKal 5.2.46)
Even from a stem ending in long '<s>ū</s>,' the <s>ūṅ</s> [feminine suffix applies], because of [its] applicability (<s>pravṛtti</s>). (VKal 5.2.47*)
The form '<s>kārtikīya</s>' — the <s>ṭhañ</s> [suffix] is difficult to sustain. (VKal 5.2.48)
And likewise '<s>śārvaram</s>' (nocturnal). (VKal 5.2.49)
'<s>Śāśvatam</s>' (eternal) — because of [established] usage (<s>prayukti</s>). (VKal 5.2.50)
[Forms like] '<s>rājavaṃśya</s>' (of royal lineage) etc. — those [suffixes] that are used in the [required] correct sense (<s>sādhvartha</s>). (VKal 5.2.51)
The word '<s>dārava</s>' (wooden) is incorrectly used (<s>duṣprayukta</s>). (VKal 5.2.52)
In [forms like] '<s>mugdhi</s>' etc., a <s>manij</s> [suffix-like form] is to be sought [to explain the derivation]. (VKal 5.2.53)
[Forms like] '<s>aupamya</s>' (comparison) etc. [are formed] like '<s>cāturvarṇya</s>' (the four-class system). (VKal 5.2.54)
Of the <s>ṣyañ</s> [suffix], because of the <s>ṣit</s> marker, the initial '<s>ī</s>' [of the base is] often [altered]. (VKal 5.2.55)
'<s>Dhanvī</s>' (archer/desert) — because of [its] listing among the '<s>vrīhi</s>' group. (VKal 5.2.56)
'<s>Caturasra</s>' (square) and '<s>śobhī</s>' (shining) — with the <s>ṇin</s> [suffix] in both. (VKal 5.2.57)
'<s>Kañcukīyā</s>' (relating to a chamberlain) — with the <s>kyac</s> [suffix]. (VKal 5.2.58)
Even when the <s>Bauddha</s> (Buddhist) [usage serves as] a counterexample, forms in the superlative (<s>ātiśāyanika</s>) [are valid depending on] context. (VKal 5.2.59)
[Forms like] '<s>kauśila</s>' etc. — with the <s>ilac</s> [suffix], through elision of a vowel (<s>varṇalopa</s>). (VKal 5.2.60)
'<s>Mauktikam</s>' (pearl) — because of [its] listing in the <s>vinaya</s> group. (VKal 5.2.61)
[Forms like] '<s>prātibha</s>' (intuitive) etc. — [formed] from '<s>prajñā</s>' (wisdom) and similar [bases]. (VKal 5.2.62)
'<s>Saraja</s>' (dusty) and '<s>samita</s>' — [these are] not <s>avyayībhāva</s> (indeclinable) compounds. (VKal 5.2.63)
'<s>Dhṛtadhanuṣī</s>' (having taken up a bow) — [this is valid] when it is not a proper name (<s>asaṃjñāyām</s>). (VKal 5.2.64)
In the word '<s>durgandhi</s>' (foul-smelling), the <s>id</s> [augment] is difficult to obtain. (VKal 5.2.65)
[Forms like] '<s>sudati</s>' (beautiful-toothed) etc. should be analyzed [individually]. (VKal 5.2.66)

children.text: kṣatadṛḍhorsa iti na kap, tadantavidhipratiṣedhāt // VKal_5,2.67* //
children.translated_text: In '<s>kṣatadṛḍhorasa</s>' (having a wounded, strong chest), the <s>kap</s> [suffix does not apply], because of the prohibition of the <s>tadanta</s> (ending-based) rule. (VKal 5.2.67*)
'<s>Avaihī</s>' — the <s>vṛddhi</s> [vowel strengthening] is faulty. (VKal 5.2.68)
'<s>Apāṅganetra</s>' (side-glancing eye) — the <s>luk</s> [elision of suffix applies], from [stems] not taking [it normally]. (VKal 5.2.69)
[Forms like] '<s>śliṣṭapriya</s>' (fond of embracing) etc. are not approved, because of the prohibition of <s>puṃvadbhāva</s> (masculine-like treatment) [for the feminine]. (VKal 5.2.70*)
'<s>Dṛḍhabhakti</s>' (of firm devotion) — [the feminine suffix applies] everywhere (<s>sarvatra</s>). (VKal 5.2.71)
[Forms like] '<s>jambulata</s>' (creeping with rose-apple) etc. — because of the rule for short [vowel]. (VKal 5.2.72)
[Forms like] '<s>tilaka</s>' (beauty mark) etc. — [are listed] in the '<s>ajirādi</s>' group. (VKal 5.2.73)
The words '<s>niśamya</s>' and '<s>niśamayya</s>' (having perceived) — because of the difference in [their underlying] root (<s>prakṛtibheda</s>). (VKal 5.2.74)
The words '<s>saṃyamya</s>' and '<s>niyamya</s>' (having restrained) — because of [the stem] being a <s>ṇijanta</s> (causative derivative). (VKal 5.2.75*)
'<s>Prapīya</s>' (having drunk) — from [the root] <s>pīṅ</s> (to drink). (VKal 5.2.76)
'<s>Dūrayati</s>' (causes to be distant) — because of the [rule's] inclusion of '<s>bahula</s>' (optionally). (VKal 5.2.77)
In [forms like] '<s>gacchati</s>' (he goes) and similar, the <s>num</s> [augment] is not prohibited. (VKal 5.2.78)
'<s>Mitreṇa goptrā</s>' (by a friend who is a protector) — because of <s>puṃvadbhāva</s> (masculine-like treatment). (VKal 5.2.79)
'<s>Vetsyasi</s>' (you will know) — because of word-division (<s>padabhaṅga</s>). (VKal 5.2.80)
The word '<s>kāmayāna</s>' (desiring) is established [as correct] if [the suffix] is beginningless (<s>anādi</s>). (VKal 5.2.81)
The words '<s>sauhṛda</s>' (friendship) and '<s>daurhṛda</s>' (longing/aversion) — [formed] with the <s>aṇ</s> [suffix] because of [the underlying form] '<s>hṛd</s>' (heart). (VKal 5.2.82)
'<s>Virama</s>' (cease!) — by virtue of being an irregular formation (<s>nipātana</s>). (VKal 5.2.83)
In [forms like] '<s>upari-upari</s>' (above and above) etc., when denoting proximity (<s>sāmīpya</s>) and reduplicated (<s>dvirukta</s>), the accusative case (<s>dvitīyā</s>) [is used]. (VKal 5.2.84)
'<s>Mandaṃ mandam</s>' (slowly, slowly) — when [used] in a sense other than manner (<s>aprakārārthatva</s>). (VKal 5.2.85)
Not '<s>nidrā-drug</s>' (sleep-distressing), because of the [unwanted] consequence of <s>bhaṣ</s>-replacement. (VKal 5.2.86*)
In '<s>niṣpanda</s>' (motionless), the [reading with] '<s>patva</s>' is to be considered. (VKal 5.2.87)
Not '<s>aṅgulisaṅga</s>' (finger-touch) [with retroflex], because of the rule for the retroflex (<s>mūrdhanya</s>) [not applying here]. (VKal 5.2.88)
By that [principle], [forms like] '<s>Avantisena</s>' etc. are explained. (VKal 5.2.89)

In '<s>Indravāhana</s>' (Indra's vehicle), retroflexion (<s>ṇatva</s>) [does not apply], because [the condition of the 'n'] being placed (<s>āhitatva</s>) is not intended (<s>avivakṣita</s>). (VKal 5.2.90*)
Thus is completed this fifth chapter (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) on practical application (<s>prāyogika</s>).
Thus is this treatise (<s>grantha</s>) completed.
